CHAPTER 18 — पर्यावरणस्य संरक्षणम् (PARYAVARANASYA SANRAKSHANAM)

Introduction — पर्यावरणं किम्?

The word पर्यावरणम् (paryavaranam) is formed from परि (pari = around, on all sides) + आवरणम् (avaranam = covering, envelope). By यण्-सन्धि the final इ of परि meets the following आ and becomes य् (इ + आ = या), giving पर्यावरणम् — 'that which covers us on all sides', i.e. the environment. The environment is the totality of earth, water, fire (energy), air and sky together with the trees, rivers, mountains, animals and birds that share this planet with us. In this lesson (NIOS Senior Secondary Sanskrit, Course 309) we study the environment through a Sanskrit lens: the पञ्चमहाभूत framework of the five great elements, the deep reverence for trees and rivers in Indian tradition, the modern problem of प्रदूषणम् (pollution) in its several forms, our duties (कर्तव्यानि) toward nature, five authentic ancient verses on nature with their word meanings and अन्वय, and grammar (सन्धि, समास, विभक्ति, कृदन्त) drawn from the text.

पञ्चमहाभूतानि — The Five Great Elements

Indian thought regards the whole material world as woven out of five great elements (पञ्चमहाभूतानि): पृथिवी (earth), आपः / जलम् (water), तेजः / अग्निः (fire, energy), वायुः (air) and आकाशः (space, sky). Our own body too is said to be पञ्चभूतात्मकम् — made of these very five elements. When the five elements remain pure and in balance, life flourishes; when they are polluted, disease and calamity follow for every living being. Protecting the environment is therefore not charity toward nature — it is the protection of the very elements out of which we ourselves are made. This is why पर्यावरणस्य संरक्षणम् (protection of the environment) is called in this lesson our धरणीधर्मः — our duty toward the Earth that bears us.

पाठ्यांशः १ — पर्यावरणस्य स्वरूपम् (original Sanskrit prose)

यत् अस्मान् परितः आवृणोति तत् पर्यावरणम् इति कथ्यते। पृथिवी जलं तेजः वायुः आकाशः इति पञ्च महाभूतानि पर्यावरणस्य मूलतत्त्वानि सन्ति। वृक्षाः नद्यः पर्वताः पशवः पक्षिणः च अस्माकं पर्यावरणस्य अङ्गानि। यदा एतानि शुद्धानि सन्ति तदा मानवः सुखं जीवति। यदा तु मानवः स्वार्थेन प्रकृतिं पीडयति तदा सः स्वयमेव दुःखं प्राप्नोति।
शब्दार्थ: परितः = on all sides; आवृणोति = covers; कथ्यते = is called; मूलतत्त्वानि = basic elements; अङ्गानि = limbs, parts; शुद्धानि = pure; स्वार्थेन = out of selfishness; पीडयति = torments, harms; स्वयमेव = he himself.
English: That which covers us on all sides is called the environment. Earth, water, fire, air and sky — these five great elements are the basic constituents of the environment. Trees, rivers, mountains, animals and birds are its limbs. When these are pure, man lives happily; but when man torments nature out of selfishness, he himself reaps the sorrow.

पाठ्यांशः २ — वृक्षाणां महिमा (the glory of trees)

वृक्षाः अस्माकं परमाः बन्धवः। ते फलानि पुष्पाणि छायां काष्ठम् औषधं च ददति। ते एव प्राणवायुं यच्छन्ति, दूषितं वायुं च गृह्णन्ति। वृक्षाः वृष्टिम् आकर्षन्ति, मृत्तिकायाः क्षरणं निवारयन्ति, पक्षिभ्यः आश्रयं ददति। अतः एव उच्यते — 'वृक्षाद् वर्षति पर्जन्यः पर्जन्यादन्नसम्भवः' इति। अस्माभिः प्रतिवर्षं वृक्षारोपणं करणीयम्, वृक्षच्छेदनं च वारणीयम्।
शब्दार्थ: बन्धवः = kinsmen, friends; छाया = shade; काष्ठम् = wood; औषधम् = medicine; प्राणवायुः = life-breath (oxygen); यच्छन्ति = give; गृह्णन्ति = take in; वृष्टिः = rain; आकर्षन्ति = attract; क्षरणम् = erosion; निवारयन्ति = prevent; आश्रयः = shelter; वृक्षारोपणम् = tree-planting; करणीयम् = should be done; वृक्षच्छेदनम् = tree-felling; वारणीयम् = should be stopped.
English: Trees are our greatest kinsmen. They give fruits, flowers, shade, wood and medicine. They alone give us the breath of life (oxygen) and absorb foul air. Trees attract rain, prevent soil erosion and shelter the birds. Hence the traditional saying — 'From the tree the rain-cloud rains; from rain arises food.' Every year we must plant trees (वृक्षारोपणम्) and stop the felling of trees.

पाठ्यांशः ३ — नद्यः जलं च (rivers and water)

भारतीयपरम्परायां नद्यः मातृवत् पूज्यन्ते — गङ्गा यमुना गोदावरी सरस्वती नर्मदा सिन्धुः कावेरी च। 'जलं जीवनम्' इति सर्वे जानन्ति — जलं विना न कृषिः, न जीवनम्। अद्य तु नगराणां मलिनजलं यन्त्रागाराणां च विषाक्तं द्रव्यं नदीषु पात्यते। तेन जलप्रदूषणं जायते, मत्स्याः म्रियन्ते, जनाः रोगैः पीड्यन्ते। अतः जलस्य मितव्ययः नदीनां शुद्धिः च अस्माकं परमं कर्तव्यम्।
शब्दार्थ: मातृवत् = like a mother; पूज्यन्ते = are worshipped; कृषिः = agriculture; मलिनजलम् = dirty water, sewage; यन्त्रागारम् = factory; विषाक्तम् = poisonous; द्रव्यम् = substance; पात्यते = is thrown; जायते = arises; मत्स्याः = fish; म्रियन्ते = die; पीड्यन्ते = are afflicted; मितव्ययः = economical (measured) use; शुद्धिः = cleansing.
English: In Indian tradition the rivers are worshipped like mothers — Ganga, Yamuna, Godavari, Saraswati, Narmada, Sindhu and Kaveri. 'Water is life' — without water there is no agriculture and no life. But today the sewage of cities and the poisonous discharge of factories are dumped into the rivers. Thus water pollution arises, fish die, and people suffer from diseases. Hence the measured use of water and the cleansing of rivers is our highest duty.

पाठ्यांशः ४ — प्रदूषणस्य प्रकाराः (kinds of pollution)

अद्य पर्यावरणस्य महती समस्या प्रदूषणम् अस्ति। तत् चतुर्विधं भवति —
(१) वायुप्रदूषणम् — यानानां धूमः, यन्त्रागाराणां धूमः, वनानां दहनं च वायुं दूषयन्ति। तेन श्वासरोगाः जायन्ते।
(२) जलप्रदूषणम् — मलिनजलं, विषाक्तरसायनानि, अवकरः च जलं दूषयन्ति। दूषितं जलं पीत्वा जनाः रोगिणः भवन्ति।
(३) ध्वनिप्रदूषणम् — यानानां ध्वनिः, उच्चैः वादित्राणि च ध्वनिप्रदूषणं जनयन्ति। तेन श्रवणशक्तिः हीयते, चित्तम् अशान्तं भवति।
(४) मृदाप्रदूषणम् — प्लास्टिकम्, रासायनिकोर्वरकाणि, अवकरः च भूमिं दूषयन्ति। तेन भूमेः उर्वरता नश्यति।
शब्दार्थ: चतुर्विधम् = of four kinds; यानम् = vehicle; धूमः = smoke; दहनम् = burning; दूषयन्ति = pollute; श्वासरोगः = respiratory disease; रसायनानि = chemicals; अवकरः = garbage; पीत्वा = having drunk; वादित्रम् = loudspeaker, instrument; जनयन्ति = produce; श्रवणशक्तिः = power of hearing; हीयते = diminishes; अशान्तम् = restless; ऊर्वरकम् = fertilizer; उर्वरता = fertility; नश्यति = perishes.
English: Today pollution is the great problem of the environment, and it is of four kinds: (1) air pollution — the smoke of vehicles and factories and the burning of forests foul the air, causing respiratory diseases; (2) water pollution — sewage, poisonous chemicals and garbage foul the water, and people fall ill by drinking it; (3) noise pollution — the din of vehicles and blaring loudspeakers weaken our hearing and make the mind restless; (4) soil pollution — plastic, chemical fertilizers and garbage foul the land, destroying its fertility.

पाठ्यांशः ५ — अस्माकं कर्तव्यानि (our duties)

वयं वृक्षान् रोपयेम, जलं मितं व्ययेम, प्लास्टिकस्य प्रयोगं त्यजेम, अवकरं यत्र तत्र न क्षिपेम, पदयात्रां द्विचक्रिकां च आद्रियेम, अन्यान् अपि पर्यावरणरक्षायै प्रेरयेम। एतत् एव अस्माकं धरणीधर्मः।
शब्दार्थ: रोपयेम = may we plant; मितम् = sparingly; व्ययेम = may we spend/use; त्यजेम = may we give up; क्षिपेम = may we throw; पदयात्रा = walking; द्विचक्रिका = bicycle; आद्रियेम = may we adopt; प्रेरयेम = may we inspire.
English: Let us plant trees, use water sparingly, give up plastic, never litter, prefer walking and cycling, and inspire others also to protect the environment. This alone is our dharma toward Mother Earth.

प्राचीनवचनानि — Five ancient verses on nature (शब्दार्थ, अन्वय, translation)

1) मत्स्यपुराणम् —
दश कूपसमा वापी दशवापीसमो ह्रदः ।
दशह्रदसमः पुत्रो दशपुत्रसमो द्रुमः ॥
शब्दार्थ: कूपः = well; समा = equal to; वापी = step-well; ह्रदः = lake, pond; पुत्रः = son; द्रुमः = tree.
अन्वय: वापी दशकूपसमा (भवति); ह्रदः दशवापीसमः; पुत्रः दशह्रदसमः; द्रुमः दशपुत्रसमः (भवति)।
Translation: One step-well equals ten wells; one lake equals ten step-wells; one son equals ten lakes; and one tree equals ten sons.
Moral: In merit, a single tree outweighs even ten sons — the ancient Indian scale of ecological value, because a tree serves all beings selflessly for generations.

2) पुराणवचनम् (on tree-planting) —
अश्वत्थमेकं पिचुमन्दमेकं न्यग्रोधमेकं दश चिञ्चिणीकान् ।
कपित्थबिल्वामलकत्रयं च पञ्चाम्रवापी नरकं न पश्येत् ॥
शब्दार्थ: अश्वत्थः = peepal; पिचुमन्दः = neem; न्यग्रोधः = banyan; चिञ्चिणी = tamarind; कपित्थः = wood-apple; बिल्वः = bael; आमलकः = amla; आम्रः = mango; नरकम् = hell; न पश्येत् = would not see.
Translation: He who plants one peepal, one neem, one banyan, ten tamarinds, three each of wood-apple, bael and amla, and five mango trees (with a well) — he never sees hell.
Moral: Tradition made tree-planting a sacred, merit-earning duty; every named tree is of medicinal or nutritional value to the whole community.

3) स्मृतिवचनम् (traditional saying) —
वृक्षाद् वर्षति पर्जन्यः पर्जन्यादन्नसम्भवः ।
शब्दार्थ: वृक्षात् = from the tree; वर्षति = rains; पर्जन्यः = rain-cloud, rain; पर्जन्यात् = from rain; अन्नसम्भवः = the arising of food.
Translation: Because of trees the rain-cloud rains; from rain arises food.
Moral: The verse states the ecological chain — trees bring rain, rain brings food, food sustains life. Cut the trees and the whole chain collapses.

4) भूमिसूक्तम् (अथर्ववेदः, काण्डः 12) —
माता भूमिः पुत्रोऽहं पृथिव्याः ।
यत् ते भूमे विखनामि क्षिप्रं तदपि रोहतु ।
मा ते मर्म विमृग्वरि मा ते हृदयमर्पिपम् ॥
शब्दार्थ: माता = mother; भूमिः = the Earth; पुत्रः = son; अहम् = I; पृथिव्याः = of the Earth; यत् = whatever; ते = of you; विखनामि = I dig; क्षिप्रम् = quickly; रोहतु = may it grow (back); मर्म = vital point; हृदयम् = heart.
Translation: 'The Earth is my mother and I am her son.' 'Whatever of you, O Earth, I dig out, may it quickly grow back again; may I never pierce your vitals or your heart.'
Moral: The Vedic seer takes only what the Earth can regenerate and vows never to wound her mortally — the world's oldest charter of sustainable, restrained use of natural resources.

5) सुभाषितम् (चाणक्यनीतिपरम्परा) —
पृथिव्यां त्रीणि रत्नानि जलमन्नं सुभाषितम् ।
मूढैः पाषाणखण्डेषु रत्नसंज्ञा विधीयते ॥
शब्दार्थ: पृथिव्याम् = on the earth; त्रीणि = three; रत्नानि = jewels; जलम् = water; अन्नम् = food; सुभाषितम् = the well-said word; मूढैः = by fools; पाषाणखण्डेषु = on pieces of stone; रत्नसंज्ञा = the name 'jewel'; विधीयते = is applied.
Translation: On this earth there are only three jewels — water, food and the well-spoken word; it is fools who give the name 'jewel' to pieces of stone.
Moral: The true wealth of the planet is what sustains life — water and food — not gold and gems; hence conserving water is guarding a jewel.

व्याकरणम् — Grammar from the text

(A) सन्धिः (joining of sounds):
  • परि + आवरणम् → पर्यावरणम् (यण्-सन्धिः: इ + आ = या).
  • पुत्रः + अहम् → पुत्रोऽहम् (विसर्ग-सन्धिः: ः + अ = ोऽ, the अवग्रह ऽ marks the elided अ).
  • वृक्षात् + वर्षति → वृक्षाद् वर्षति (जश्त्व-सन्धिः: त् → द् before a voiced sound).
  • पर्जन्यात् + अन्नसम्भवः → पर्जन्यादन्नसम्भवः (त् → द् again).
  • दशपुत्रसमः + द्रुमः → दशपुत्रसमो द्रुमः (विसर्ग-सन्धिः: ः → ओ before a voiced consonant).
  • न + अस्ति → नास्ति (सवर्णदीर्घ-सन्धिः: अ + अ = आ); जलम् + अन्नम् → जलमन्नम्.

(B) समासः (compounds):
  • जलप्रदूषणम् = जलस्य प्रदूषणम् (षष्ठी-तत्पुरुषः); likewise वायुप्रदूषणम्, ध्वनिप्रदूषणम्, मृदाप्रदूषणम्.
  • वृक्षारोपणम् = वृक्षाणाम् आरोपणम् (षष्ठी-तत्पुरुषः); नदीसंरक्षणम् = नद्याः संरक्षणम्.
  • महाभूतम् = महत् च तत् भूतम् (कर्मधारयः); पञ्चमहाभूतानि counts five of them (द्विगु-flavoured compound).
  • कूपसमा = कूपैः समा (तृतीया-तत्पुरुषः) — 'equal to (ten) wells'.

(C) विभक्तिः (case endings) from the text:
  • वृक्षात् — पञ्चमी ('from the tree'); पर्जन्यात् — पञ्चमी ('from rain').
  • पृथिव्याः — षष्ठी ('of the Earth', in पुत्रोऽहं पृथिव्याः); पृथिव्याम् — सप्तमी ('on the earth').
  • जलेन — तृतीया ('by water'); नदीषु — सप्तमी बहुवचनम् ('in the rivers'); पक्षिभ्यः — चतुर्थी ('for the birds').
  • हे भूमे — सम्बोधनम् (vocative, 'O Earth!', as in यत् ते भूमे विखनामि).

(D) कृदन्ताः (participles and verbal derivatives):
  • तुमुन् (infinitive): रक्षितुम् = 'in order to protect' — पर्यावरणं रक्षितुं वयं वृक्षान् रोपयामः।
  • क्त्वा (absolutive): रोपयित्वा = 'having planted' — वृक्षान् रोपयित्वा सः जलम् अयच्छत्; पीत्वा = 'having drunk'.
  • ल्यप् (absolutive with prefix): संरक्ष्य = 'having protected' — नदीं संरक्ष्य ग्रामः सुखी अभवत्।
  • क्त (past passive participle): प्रदूषितम् = 'polluted'; रक्षितम् = 'protected'.

SUMMARY (सारांश)

You learned that पर्यावरणम् (परि + आवरणम्, यण्-सन्धि) is 'that which covers us on all sides', built of the पञ्चमहाभूतानि of which our body too is made; read prose on trees, rivers, the four pollutions and our duties; studied five ancient verses — 'दशपुत्रसमो द्रुमः', the tree-planting verse ('नरकं न पश्येत्'), 'वृक्षाद् वर्षति पर्जन्यः', the भूमिसूक्त lines, and 'पृथिव्यां त्रीणि रत्नानि'; and drew from the text its सन्धि, समास, विभक्ति and कृदन्त. The Earth is our mother; her protection is our धरणीधर्मः.

topics.name: पर्यावरणम् — Meaning and the पञ्चमहाभूत Framework
topics.description: The formation and meaning of पर्यावरणम् (परि + आवरणम्, यण्-सन्धि) and the Indian framework of the five great elements — पृथिवी, आपः, तेजः, वायुः, आकाशः — of which the world and our own body (पञ्चभूतात्मकम्) are made.

topics.name: Sacredness of Trees and Rivers in Indian Tradition
topics.description: The glory of trees (वृक्षाणां महिमा) and the motherly sanctity of rivers (नद्यः मातृवत् पूज्यन्ते) in Indian tradition — गङ्गा, यमुना and other rivers, tree-planting as sacred merit, and the ecological wisdom hidden in this reverence.

topics.name: प्रदूषणम् — Types, Causes and Effects of Pollution
topics.description: The four kinds of pollution — वायुप्रदूषणम्, जलप्रदूषणम्, ध्वनिप्रदूषणम् and मृदाप्रदूषणम् — their causes (vehicle and factory smoke, sewage, loudspeakers, plastic, chemical fertilizers) and their effects on health, water life and soil fertility.

chapter_summary.title: पर्यावरणस्य संरक्षणम् (Paryavaranasya Sanrakshanam) — Chapter Summary
chapter_summary.intro: This NIOS Senior Secondary Sanskrit (309) summary for Chapter 18 views environmental protection through a Sanskrit lens: the five great elements (पञ्चमहाभूत), the sacredness of trees and rivers, the four kinds of pollution, our duties toward nature, five authentic ancient verses, and grammar drawn from the text.

branches.label: पञ्चमहाभूतानि — Five Elements
details: शरीरं पञ्चभूतात्मकम् — the body itself is made of them

branches.label: वृक्षाः नद्यः च — Trees & Rivers
details: दशपुत्रसमो द्रुमः — one tree = ten sons
वृक्षाद् वर्षति पर्जन्यः — trees bring rain
नद्यः मातृवत् पूज्यन्ते — rivers as mothers

branches.label: कर्तव्यानि — Duties
details: Walk, cycle, and inspire others — धरणीधर्मः

sections.heading: पर्यावरणम् and the five great elements
bullets: पर्यावरणम् = परि (around) + आवरणम् (covering), joined by यण्-सन्धि (इ + आ = या): 'that which covers us on all sides'.
The material world is woven of the पञ्चमहाभूतानि — पृथिवी, आपः, तेजः, वायुः, आकाशः — and our body too is पञ्चभूतात्मकम्.
When the five elements are pure and balanced, life flourishes; when they are polluted, disease and calamity follow.
Environmental protection is therefore self-protection — the lesson calls it धरणीधर्मः, our duty toward the Earth.

sections.heading: The glory of trees and sanctity of rivers
bullets: Trees give fruits, flowers, shade, wood, medicine and oxygen (प्राणवायुः); they attract rain, stop soil erosion and shelter birds.
The Matsya Purana ladder ends दशपुत्रसमो द्रुमः — a single tree outweighs ten sons in merit.
The Purana tree-planting verse promises that he who plants peepal, neem, banyan, tamarind and fruit trees 'नरकं न पश्येत्' — never sees hell.
Rivers — गङ्गा, यमुना, गोदावरी, नर्मदा, कावेरी — are worshipped like mothers (मातृवत्), and the भूमिसूक्त declares माता भूमिः पुत्रोऽहं पृथिव्याः.

sections.heading: The four kinds of pollution
bullets: वायुप्रदूषणम्: smoke of vehicles (यानानां धूमः) and factories and forest-burning foul the air, causing श्वासरोगाः (respiratory diseases).
जलप्रदूषणम्: sewage (मलिनजलम्), toxic chemicals and garbage dumped into rivers kill fish and sicken people.
ध्वनिप्रदूषणम्: the din of vehicles and loudspeakers weakens hearing (श्रवणशक्तिः हीयते) and makes the mind restless.
मृदाप्रदूषणम्: plastic, chemical fertilizers and garbage destroy the fertility (उर्वरता) of the soil.

sections.heading: Verses of ecological wisdom
bullets: दश कूपसमा वापी... दशपुत्रसमो द्रुमः (Matsya Purana): step-well > wells, lake > step-wells, son > lakes, tree > sons.
वृक्षाद् वर्षति पर्जन्यः पर्जन्यादन्नसम्भवः: trees bring rain, rain brings food — the chain of life.
भूमिसूक्तम् (Atharvaveda): यत् ते भूमे विखनामि क्षिप्रं तदपि रोहतु — take only what the Earth can regrow; never pierce her vitals.
पृथिव्यां त्रीणि रत्नानि जलमन्नं सुभाषितम्: water, food and the well-said word are earth's only true jewels.

sections.heading: Grammar from the text
bullets: सन्धिः: परि + आवरणम् = पर्यावरणम् (यण्); पुत्रः + अहम् = पुत्रोऽहम् (विसर्ग); वृक्षात् + वर्षति = वृक्षाद् वर्षति (जश्त्व); न + अस्ति = नास्ति (दीर्घ).
समासः: जलप्रदूषणम् = जलस्य प्रदूषणम् and वृक्षारोपणम् = वृक्षाणाम् आरोपणम् (both षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष); महाभूतम् = महत् च तत् भूतम् (कर्मधारय).
विभक्तिः: वृक्षात् (पञ्चमी), पृथिव्याः (षष्ठी), पृथिव्याम्/नदीषु (सप्तमी), जलेन (तृतीया), पक्षिभ्यः (चतुर्थी), हे भूमे (सम्बोधन).
कृदन्ताः: रक्षितुम् (तुमुन्), रोपयित्वा/पीत्वा (क्त्वा), संरक्ष्य (ल्यप्), प्रदूषितम्/रक्षितम् (क्त).

key_takeaways: पर्यावरणम् (परि + आवरणम्, यण्-सन्धि) is 'that which covers us on all sides' — the five elements together with all living beings.
The body itself is पञ्चभूतात्मकम् — made of the five elements — so polluting the elements is poisoning ourselves.
One tree equals ten sons (दशपुत्रसमो द्रुमः, Matsya Purana), and planting trees is a sacred, merit-earning duty.
Trees bring rain and rain brings food — वृक्षाद् वर्षति पर्जन्यः पर्जन्यादन्नसम्भवः — so tree-felling breaks the chain of life.
The भूमिसूक्त teaches sustainable use: dig only what can quickly regrow, and never pierce the Earth-mother's vitals.
Pollution is fourfold — वायु, जल, ध्वनि and मृदा — caused by smoke, sewage, noise and plastic, harming breath, water, hearing and soil.
Our धरणीधर्मः: plant trees, use water sparingly, refuse plastic, never litter, walk or cycle, and inspire others.

glossary.definition: The environment — 'that which covers on all sides', from परि (around) + आवरणम् (covering), joined by यण्-सन्धि.
Protection, conservation; पर्यावरणस्य संरक्षणम् is the protection of the environment.
The five great elements — पृथिवी (earth), आपः (water), तेजः (fire), वायुः (air), आकाशः (space) — of which the world and body are made.
Pollution — the fouling of air, water, sound-environment or soil; in the lesson it is चतुर्विधम् (of four kinds).
Tree-planting (वृक्षाणाम् आरोपणम्, षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष compound) — the foremost duty of environmental protection.
A tree; in the Matsya Purana verse, दशपुत्रसमो द्रुमः — one tree equals ten sons in merit.
A step-well; in the verse, one step-well equals ten ordinary wells (दश कूपसमा वापी).
The rain-cloud or rain; वृक्षाद् वर्षति पर्जन्यः — because of trees the rain-cloud rains.
The Hymn to the Earth in the Atharvaveda, source of माता भूमिः पुत्रोऽहं पृथिव्याः — 'Earth is my mother, I am her son'.
Dirty water, sewage — the waste water of cities that pollutes rivers when dumped into them.
Garbage, refuse — a cause of both water pollution and soil pollution when thrown carelessly.
Measured, economical use; जलस्य मितव्ययः — using water sparingly — is a key conservation duty.
Respiratory disease — the chief effect of air pollution (वायुप्रदूषणम्) caused by vehicle and factory smoke.
'The dharma toward the Earth-bearer' — the lesson's name for our collective duty to protect the environment.
The peepal (sacred fig) tree — first of the trees named in the Purana tree-planting verse.

worksheet.title: Worksheet — पर्यावरणस्य संरक्षणम् (Paryavaranasya Sanrakshanam)
worksheet.instructions: Answer all questions. Write Sanskrit answers in Devanagari where asked. For MCQs choose the single best option. Marks for each question are shown against it.

questions.question:
Translate the following verse into simple English and state its moral:
दश कूपसमा वापी दशवापीसमो ह्रदः ।
दशह्रदसमः पुत्रो दशपुत्रसमो द्रुमः ॥
questions.answer: One step-well (वापी) equals ten wells (कूप); one lake (ह्रदः) equals ten step-wells; one son (पुत्रः) equals ten lakes; and one tree (द्रुमः) equals ten sons. Moral: in merit a single tree outweighs even ten sons, because it serves all beings selflessly for generations — the ancient scale of ecological value.
questions.explanation: The Matsya Purana verse ranks water-bodies, sons and trees on a ladder of public merit, placing the tree highest.

questions.question: पर्यावरणम् इत्यस्य सन्धिविच्छेदः कः?
questions.explanation: परि + आवरणम् = पर्यावरणम् by यण्-सन्धि (इ + आ = या).

questions.question: पृथिवी जलं तेजः वायुः आकाशः इति ____ महाभूतानि सन्ति।
questions.explanation: There are five (पञ्च) great elements — the पञ्चमहाभूतानि.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ (English word meaning) of each: द्रुमः, वापी, पर्जन्यः, अवकरः, मितव्ययः.
questions.answer: द्रुमः = tree; वापी = step-well; पर्जन्यः = rain-cloud / rain; अवकरः = garbage, refuse; मितव्ययः = measured / economical use.
questions.explanation: Core vocabulary drawn from the verses and prose of the chapter.

questions.question: ध्वनिप्रदूषणेन श्रवणशक्तिः हीयते चित्तम् च अशान्तं भवति।
questions.explanation: The lesson states that noise pollution weakens hearing and makes the mind restless.

questions.question: Name the four kinds of प्रदूषणम् described in the lesson (in Sanskrit) and give one cause of each.
questions.answer: (1) वायुप्रदूषणम् — smoke of vehicles and factories (यानानां यन्त्रागाराणां च धूमः); (2) जलप्रदूषणम् — sewage and toxic chemicals dumped into rivers (मलिनजलम्, विषाक्तरसायनानि); (3) ध्वनिप्रदूषणम् — din of vehicles and loudspeakers (यानध्वनिः, उच्चैः वादित्राणि); (4) मृदाप्रदूषणम् — plastic and chemical fertilizers (प्लास्टिकम्, रासायनिकोर्वरकाणि).
questions.explanation: The chapter's fourfold classification of pollution with its principal causes.

questions.question: 'माता भूमिः पुत्रोऽहं पृथिव्याः' इति वचनं कुत्र वर्तते?
questions.explanation: The line 'Earth is my mother, I am her son' is from the Bhumi Sukta (Hymn to the Earth) of the Atharvaveda.

questions.question:
Read the भूमिसूक्त lines and answer:
माता भूमिः पुत्रोऽहं पृथिव्याः ।
यत् ते भूमे विखनामि क्षिप्रं तदपि रोहतु ।
मा ते मर्म विमृग्वरि मा ते हृदयमर्पिपम् ॥
(a) What relationship does the seer declare with the Earth? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of विखनामि and रोहतु. (c) Which विभक्ति is पृथिव्याः? (d) What environmental principle do these lines teach?
questions.answer: (a) The Earth is his mother and he is her son (माता भूमिः, पुत्रः अहम्). (b) विखनामि = 'I dig out'; रोहतु = 'may it grow (back)'. (c) पृथिव्याः is षष्ठी (genitive) — 'of the Earth'. (d) The principle of sustainable, restrained use: take from the Earth only what can quickly regenerate, and never wound her vitally — the oldest charter of resource conservation.
questions.explanation: Comprehension of the Vedic hymn: relationship, vocabulary, case and ecological ethic.

questions.question: 'वृक्षारोपणं परमं कर्तव्यम्' — Explain the importance of trees according to this chapter (their gifts, their role in rain and soil, the Purana verses about them), and describe the duties the lesson lays down for protecting the environment.
questions.answer: Trees are our greatest kinsmen (परमाः बन्धवः): they give fruits, flowers, shade, wood and medicine; they give oxygen (प्राणवायुः) and absorb foul air; they attract rain, prevent soil erosion and shelter birds. The chain-verse says वृक्षाद् वर्षति पर्जन्यः पर्जन्यादन्नसम्भवः — trees bring rain and rain brings food, so felling trees breaks the chain of life. The Matsya Purana ranks one tree above ten sons (दशपुत्रसमो द्रुमः), and another Purana verse promises that he who plants a peepal, a neem, a banyan, ten tamarinds, three each of kapittha–bilva–amalaka and five mangoes 'नरकं न पश्येत्' — never sees hell. Hence the duties: plant trees every year (वृक्षारोपणम्) and stop tree-felling; use water sparingly (जलस्य मितव्ययः) and keep rivers clean; give up plastic; never litter; prefer walking and cycling; and inspire others to protect the environment. This is our धरणीधर्मः — the dharma we owe to Mother Earth.
questions.explanation: Draws together the tree-glory prose, the three tree-verses and the duties paragraph of the lesson.

questions.question: From the chapter, (a) split the सन्धि: पर्यावरणम्, पुत्रोऽहम्, वृक्षाद् वर्षति, नास्ति; (b) give the विग्रह and name of the समास: जलप्रदूषणम्, वृक्षारोपणम्; (c) state the विभक्ति of: वृक्षात्, नदीषु; (d) identify the कृदन्त type of: रक्षितुम्, रोपयित्वा.
questions.answer: (a) पर्यावरणम् = परि + आवरणम् (यण्-सन्धिः); पुत्रोऽहम् = पुत्रः + अहम् (विसर्ग-सन्धिः, ोऽ); वृक्षाद् वर्षति = वृक्षात् + वर्षति (जश्त्व, त् → द्); नास्ति = न + अस्ति (सवर्णदीर्घ-सन्धिः). (b) जलप्रदूषणम् = जलस्य प्रदूषणम् — षष्ठी-तत्पुरुषः; वृक्षारोपणम् = वृक्षाणाम् आरोपणम् — षष्ठी-तत्पुरुषः. (c) वृक्षात् — पञ्चमी ('from the tree'); नदीषु — सप्तमी बहुवचनम् ('in the rivers'). (d) रक्षितुम् — तुमुन् (infinitive, 'in order to protect'); रोपयित्वा — क्त्वा (absolutive, 'having planted').
questions.explanation: Covers all four grammar strands of the chapter: sandhi, samasa, vibhakti and kridanta.

questions.question: पर्यावरणम् इति पदस्य सन्धिविच्छेदः कः?
questions.explanation: परि (around) + आवरणम् (covering) join by यण्-सन्धि to give पर्यावरणम्.

questions.question: महाभूतानि सङ्ख्यया कति सन्ति?
questions.explanation: The great elements are five — पृथिवी, आपः, तेजः, वायुः, आकाशः.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the पञ्चमहाभूतानि?
questions.explanation: मनः (mind) is not a महाभूत; the five are पृथिवी, आपः, तेजः, वायुः and आकाशः.

questions.question: 'आपः' इति महाभूतस्य अर्थः कः?
questions.explanation: आपः (also जलम्) is the water element among the five great elements.

questions.question: अस्माकं शरीरं किम् इति उच्यते?
questions.explanation: The body is said to be made of the very five elements — पञ्चभूतात्मकम्.

questions.question: 'तेजः' इति महाभूतं कस्य अपरं नाम?
questions.explanation: तेजः is the fire/energy element, another name for अग्निः.

questions.question: पाठे उक्तम् — 'यत् अस्मान् परितः आवृणोति तत् ____ इति कथ्यते।'
questions.explanation: That which covers us on all sides is called the environment (पर्यावरणम्).

questions.question: 'परितः' इत्यस्य शब्दार्थः कः?
questions.explanation: परितः means 'around, on all sides' — the environment surrounds us on all sides.

questions.question: Which महाभूत means 'space / sky'?
questions.explanation: आकाशः is the space (sky/ether) element.

questions.question: According to the lesson, what follows when the five elements become polluted?
options: Disease and calamity for all living beings
questions.answer: Disease and calamity for all living beings
questions.explanation: When the elements are impure and unbalanced, disease and calamity follow for every living being.

questions.question: The lesson says protecting the environment is really the protection of what?
options: The five elements of which we ourselves are made
questions.answer: The five elements of which we ourselves are made
questions.explanation: Since the body is पञ्चभूतात्मकम्, protecting the elements is protecting ourselves.

questions.question: यदा मानवः स्वार्थेन प्रकृतिं पीडयति तदा किं भवति इति पाठे उक्तम्?
questions.explanation: When man torments nature out of selfishness, he himself reaps the sorrow.

questions.question: 'दश कूपसमा वापी दशवापीसमो ह्रदः...' इति श्लोकः कस्मात् ग्रन्थात् गृहीतः?
questions.explanation: The ladder-verse ending दशपुत्रसमो द्रुमः is from the Matsya Purana.

questions.question: According to the Matsya Purana verse, one tree (द्रुमः) is equal to how many sons?
questions.explanation: दशपुत्रसमो द्रुमः — one tree equals ten sons.

questions.question: श्लोकानुसारं 'दशवापीसमः' कः अस्ति?
questions.explanation: दशवापीसमो ह्रदः — one lake equals ten step-wells.

questions.question: Complete the verse: दशह्रदसमः पुत्रो दशपुत्रसमो ____ ॥
questions.explanation: The verse ends दशपुत्रसमो द्रुमः — one tree equals ten sons.

questions.question: 'माता भूमिः पुत्रोऽहं पृथिव्याः' इति वचनं कस्य वेदस्य भूमिसूक्ते अस्ति?
questions.explanation: The Bhumi Sukta (Hymn to the Earth) is in the Atharvaveda.

questions.question: In 'यत् ते भूमे विखनामि क्षिप्रं तदपि रोहतु', the seer prays that whatever he digs may —
questions.explanation: क्षिप्रं तदपि रोहतु — 'may that too quickly grow (back)': take only what regenerates.

questions.question: Complete the traditional saying: वृक्षाद् वर्षति पर्जन्यः ____ ।
questions.explanation: Because of trees the rain-cloud rains; from rain arises food (अन्नसम्भवः).

questions.question: 'पृथिव्यां त्रीणि रत्नानि' इति श्लोके कानि त्रीणि रत्नानि?
questions.explanation: Water, food and the well-said word are the earth's three jewels.

questions.question: अश्वत्थमेकं... इति श्लोके कति चिञ्चिणीकाः (tamarind trees) रोपणीयाः?
questions.explanation: दश चिञ्चिणीकान् — ten tamarind trees are to be planted.

questions.question: According to the tree-planting verse, one who plants the listed trees नरकं —
questions.explanation: पञ्चाम्रवापी नरकं न पश्येत् — the tree-planter never sees hell.

questions.question: 'अश्वत्थः' इति कस्य वृक्षस्य नाम?
questions.explanation: अश्वत्थः is the peepal tree; पिचुमन्दः is neem and न्यग्रोधः is banyan.

questions.question: श्लोकानुसारं मूढाः केषु 'रत्नम्' इति संज्ञां विदधति?
questions.explanation: मूढैः पाषाणखण्डेषु रत्नसंज्ञा विधीयते — fools call mere pieces of stone 'jewels'.

questions.question: पाठानुसारं प्रदूषणं कतिविधम्?
questions.explanation: Pollution in the lesson is fourfold: वायु-, जल-, ध्वनि- and मृदा-प्रदूषणम्.

questions.question: यानानां यन्त्रागाराणां च धूमेन किं प्रदूषणं जायते?
questions.explanation: The smoke of vehicles and factories causes air pollution.

questions.question: नगराणां मलिनजलं नदीषु पातनेन किं जायते?
questions.explanation: Dumping city sewage into rivers causes water pollution.

questions.question: ध्वनिप्रदूषणेन का शक्तिः हीयते?
questions.explanation: Noise pollution diminishes the power of hearing (श्रवणशक्तिः).

questions.question: वायुप्रदूषणेन के रोगाः जायन्ते इति पाठे उक्तम्?
questions.explanation: Air pollution gives rise to respiratory diseases (श्वासरोगाः).

questions.question: 'प्रदूषणम्' इत्यस्य आङ्ग्लभाषायाम् अर्थः कः?
questions.explanation: प्रदूषणम् means pollution — the fouling of air, water, sound or soil.

questions.question: मृदाप्रदूषणस्य कारणं किम् इति पाठे उक्तम्?
questions.explanation: Plastic and chemical fertilizers pollute the soil and destroy its fertility.

questions.question: जलप्रदूषणेन के म्रियन्ते इति पाठे उक्तम्?
questions.explanation: Because of water pollution the fish (मत्स्याः) die.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a cause of air pollution mentioned in the lesson?
questions.explanation: Tree-planting is a remedy, not a cause; the causes are vehicle smoke, factory smoke and forest burning.

questions.question: उच्चैः वादित्राणि यानध्वनिः च किं प्रदूषणं जनयन्ति?
questions.explanation: Loudspeakers and vehicle noise produce noise pollution.

questions.question: 'विषाक्तं द्रव्यम्' इत्यस्य अर्थः कः?
questions.explanation: विषाक्तम् = poisonous, द्रव्यम् = substance — the toxic discharge of factories.

questions.question: ध्वनिप्रदूषणेन चित्तं कीदृशं भवति?
questions.explanation: Noise pollution makes the mind restless (अशान्तम्).

questions.question: 'द्रुमः' इत्यस्य शब्दार्थः कः?
questions.explanation: द्रुमः is a synonym of वृक्षः — a tree.

questions.question: 'पर्जन्यः' इत्यस्य शब्दार्थः कः?
questions.explanation: पर्जन्यः is the rain-cloud (also the rain it gives).

questions.question: 'वापी' इत्यस्य शब्दार्थः कः?
questions.explanation: वापी is a step-well; कूपः is an ordinary well and ह्रदः a lake.

questions.question: 'आवरणम्' इत्यस्य शब्दार्थः कः?
questions.explanation: आवरणम् = covering, envelope; hence पर्यावरणम् = the all-around covering.

questions.question: 'अवकरः' इत्यस्य शब्दार्थः कः?
questions.explanation: अवकरः = garbage, refuse — a cause of water and soil pollution.

questions.question: 'यन्त्रागारम्' इत्यस्य शब्दार्थः कः?
questions.explanation: यन्त्रागारम् (यन्त्र + आगारम्, house of machines) = factory.

questions.question: 'क्षिप्रम्' इत्यस्य शब्दार्थः कः?
questions.explanation: क्षिप्रम् = quickly; क्षिप्रं तदपि रोहतु — may it quickly grow back.

questions.question: 'मर्म' इत्यस्य शब्दार्थः कः (भूमिसूक्ते 'मा ते मर्म...' इति)?
questions.explanation: मर्म = a vital, mortal spot; the seer vows never to pierce the Earth's vitals.

questions.question: 'पिचुमन्दः' इति कस्य वृक्षस्य नाम?
questions.explanation: पिचुमन्दः (also निम्बः) is the neem tree.

questions.question: 'ह्रदः' इत्यस्य शब्दार्थः कः?
questions.explanation: ह्रदः = a lake or deep pond; दशवापीसमो ह्रदः.

questions.question: 'मितव्ययः' इत्यस्य अर्थः कः?
questions.explanation: मित (measured) + व्ययः (spending) — using a resource sparingly.

questions.question: 'निवारयन्ति' इत्यस्य शब्दार्थः कः?
questions.explanation: निवारयन्ति = they ward off / prevent; trees prevent soil erosion.

questions.question: 'नद्यः मातृवत् पूज्यन्ते' — this attitude of Indian tradition chiefly expresses —
options: reverent gratitude that makes protecting rivers a sacred duty
the commercial value of river water
a mere poetic decoration with no meaning
questions.answer: reverent gratitude that makes protecting rivers a sacred duty
questions.explanation: Worshipping rivers as mothers encodes gratitude for life-giving water and binds people to protect them.

questions.question: Why does the Matsya Purana verse rank one tree above even ten sons?
options: A tree serves all beings selflessly for generations, beyond one family
Trees are costlier than raising sons
questions.answer: A tree serves all beings selflessly for generations, beyond one family
questions.explanation: A son benefits one family, but a tree gives shade, fruit, rain and shelter to all beings for a very long time.

questions.question: The भूमिसूक्त prayer 'यत् ते भूमे विखनामि क्षिप्रं तदपि रोहतु' embodies which modern principle?
options: sustainable / restrained use of natural resources
questions.answer: sustainable / restrained use of natural resources
questions.explanation: Take only what the Earth can regenerate — the essence of sustainability.

questions.question: Calling the Earth माता (mother) implies that human beings should —
options: protect and serve her as a son protects his mother
leave the Earth and settle elsewhere
questions.answer: protect and serve her as a son protects his mother
questions.explanation: The mother–son relation (माता भूमिः पुत्रोऽहम्) makes care of the Earth a filial duty.

questions.question: By promising 'नरकं न पश्येत्' to the tree-planter, tradition was effectively —
options: using religious merit to motivate environmental action
describing an actual journey to hell
questions.answer: using religious merit to motivate environmental action
questions.explanation: Attaching spiritual reward to tree-planting turned conservation into a living social practice.

questions.question: By counting जलम् and अन्नम् (not gold) among the earth's three jewels, the subhashita teaches that —
options: the true wealth of the planet is what sustains life
food and water have no value
questions.answer: the true wealth of the planet is what sustains life
questions.explanation: Water and food sustain life; stones called 'jewels' do not — so conserving water is guarding real wealth.

questions.question: The famous line 'परोपकाराय फलन्ति वृक्षाः' (trees bear fruit for others) parallels which idea of this chapter?
options: Trees are selfless benefactors, hence worth more than ten sons
Trees should be cut for wood
questions.answer: Trees are selfless benefactors, hence worth more than ten sons
questions.explanation: Both verses present the tree as the model of selfless service to all beings.

questions.question: 'पुत्रोऽहम्' इत्यस्य सन्धिविच्छेदः कः?
questions.explanation: विसर्ग-सन्धि: ः + अ → ोऽ; the अवग्रह (ऽ) marks the elided अ.

questions.question: 'वृक्षाद् वर्षति' इत्यत्र सन्धिविच्छेदः कः?
questions.explanation: जश्त्व-सन्धि: the त् of वृक्षात् becomes द् before the voiced व्.

questions.question: 'दशपुत्रसमो द्रुमः' इत्यत्र 'समो' इति रूपं केन सन्धिना जातम्?
questions.explanation: Before a voiced consonant the visarga after अ becomes ओ: समः + द्रुमः = समो द्रुमः.

questions.question: 'जलप्रदूषणम्' इत्यस्य विग्रहः कः, समासः च कः?
questions.explanation: The pollution OF water — genitive tatpurusha.

questions.question: 'वृक्षारोपणम्' = वृक्षाणाम् आरोपणम् — अयं कः समासः?
questions.explanation: 'The planting OF trees' — genitive (षष्ठी) tatpurusha compound.

questions.question: 'महाभूतम्' = महत् च तत् भूतम् — अयं कः समासः?
questions.explanation: Adjective + noun in apposition ('that which is great AND an element') — karmadharaya.

questions.question: परि + आवरणम् = पर्यावरणम् — अयं कः सन्धिः?
questions.explanation: इ + आ → या (the vowel इ becomes the semivowel य्) — yan sandhi.

questions.question: 'पर्जन्यादन्नसम्भवः' इत्यस्य प्रथमः सन्धिविच्छेदः कः?
questions.explanation: The final त् of पर्जन्यात् becomes द् before the vowel अ (जश्त्व).

questions.question: न + अस्ति = नास्ति — अयं कः सन्धिः?
questions.explanation: अ + अ merge into the long आ — savarna-dirgha sandhi.

questions.question: 'कूपसमा' (दश कूपसमा वापी) इत्यस्य विग्रहः 'कूपैः समा' इति — अयं कः समासः?
questions.explanation: 'Equal TO/WITH the wells' — instrumental (तृतीया) tatpurusha.

questions.question: 'वृक्षात्' (वृक्षाद् वर्षति पर्जन्यः) इति पदे का विभक्तिः?
questions.explanation: वृक्षात् = 'from the tree' — ablative (पञ्चमी) singular.

questions.question: 'पुत्रोऽहं पृथिव्याः' इत्यत्र 'पृथिव्याः' इति पदे का विभक्तिः?
questions.explanation: पृथिव्याः = 'of the Earth' — genitive (षष्ठी): 'I am the son of the Earth'.

questions.question: 'नदीषु' (मलिनजलं नदीषु पात्यते) इति पदे का विभक्तिः किं वचनं च?
questions.explanation: नदीषु = 'in the rivers' — locative (सप्तमी) plural.

questions.question: 'रक्षितुम्' (पर्यावरणं रक्षितुम्) इति कः कृदन्तप्रत्ययः?
questions.explanation: रक्षितुम् = 'in order to protect' — the infinitive suffix तुमुन्.

questions.question: 'रोपयित्वा' (वृक्षान् रोपयित्वा) इति कः कृदन्तप्रत्ययः?
questions.explanation: रोपयित्वा = 'having planted' — the absolutive suffix क्त्वा.

questions.question: 'जलेन' इति पदे का विभक्तिः?
questions.explanation: जलेन = 'by/with water' — instrumental (तृतीया) singular.

questions.question: 'यत् ते भूमे विखनामि' इत्यत्र 'भूमे' इति पदे का विभक्तिः?
questions.explanation: हे भूमे — 'O Earth!' — the vocative (सम्बोधन) form of भूमिः.

questions.question: 'वयं वृक्षान् रोपयेम' इत्यस्य समीचीनः आङ्ग्लानुवादः कः?
questions.explanation: रोपयेम is the optative ('may we plant') — a gentle exhortation to plant trees.

questions.question: Which action best follows the chapter's teaching against ध्वनिप्रदूषणम्?
options: Avoiding needless honking and blaring loudspeakers
questions.answer: Avoiding needless honking and blaring loudspeakers
questions.explanation: Noise pollution is curbed by restraining vehicle noise and loudspeakers.

questions.question: पाठानुसारं 'धरणीधर्मः' इत्यस्य आशयः कः?
options: Our duty toward the Earth — protecting the environment
A tax paid to the king
A festival of the rainy season
questions.answer: Our duty toward the Earth — protecting the environment
questions.explanation: The lesson names the sum of our conservation duties धरणीधर्मः — the dharma owed to Mother Earth.

questions.question: आकाशः पञ्चमहाभूतेषु अन्यतमः अस्ति।
questions.explanation: आकाशः (space) is indeed one of the five great elements.

questions.question: 'पर्यावरणम्' इति पदं परा + वरणम् इति विच्छेदेन सिद्धम्।
questions.explanation: The correct split is परि + आवरणम् (यण्-सन्धि), not परा + वरणम्.

questions.question: मत्स्यपुराणश्लोकानुसारं दश द्रुमाः एकपुत्रसमाः भवन्ति।
questions.explanation: It is the reverse — one tree equals ten sons (दशपुत्रसमो द्रुमः).

questions.question: यानानां धूमः जलप्रदूषणं जनयति।
questions.explanation: Vehicle smoke causes AIR pollution (वायुप्रदूषणम्), not water pollution.

questions.question: मृदाप्रदूषणेन भूमेः उर्वरता नश्यति।
questions.explanation: Soil pollution (plastic, chemical fertilizers) destroys the fertility of the land.

questions.question: 'द्रुमः' इत्यस्य अर्थः 'नदी' इति।
questions.explanation: द्रुमः means 'tree' (a synonym of वृक्षः); नदी is a river.

questions.question: भूमिसूक्ते पृथिवी माता इति उच्यते, वयं च तस्याः पुत्राः।
questions.explanation: माता भूमिः पुत्रोऽहं पृथिव्याः — Earth is the mother, we are her children.

questions.question: 'वृक्षाद् वर्षति' इत्यत्र वृक्षात् इति पदस्य त्-कारः द्-कारे परिवर्तितः (जश्त्व-सन्धिः)।
questions.explanation: Before the voiced व् the final त् becomes द् — jashtva sandhi.

questions.question: 'रक्षितुम्' इति क्त्वा-प्रत्ययान्तं रूपम् अस्ति।
questions.explanation: रक्षितुम् is the तुमुन् (infinitive) form; the क्त्वा form would be रक्षित्वा.

questions.question: According to the lesson, throwing plastic and garbage into rivers is part of our धरणीधर्मः.
questions.explanation: धरणीधर्मः is the opposite — giving up plastic, never littering, and keeping rivers clean.

questions.question: पर्यावरणम् = परि + ____ ।
questions.explanation: परि (around) + आवरणम् (covering) = पर्यावरणम् by यण्-सन्धि.

questions.question: महाभूतानि सङ्ख्यया ____ सन्ति (Sanskrit numeral in words)।
questions.explanation: The great elements are five — पञ्च महाभूतानि.

questions.question: Complete the verse: दशह्रदसमः पुत्रो दशपुत्रसमो ____ ॥
questions.explanation: दशपुत्रसमो द्रुमः — one tree equals ten sons.

questions.question: Complete the भूमिसूक्त line: माता ____ पुत्रोऽहं पृथिव्याः।
questions.explanation: माता भूमिः पुत्रोऽहं पृथिव्याः — 'The Earth is my mother, I am her son.'

questions.question: Complete the saying: वृक्षाद् वर्षति ____ पर्जन्यादन्नसम्भवः।
questions.explanation: वृक्षाद् वर्षति पर्जन्यः — because of trees the rain-cloud rains.

questions.question: यानानां धूमेन ____-प्रदूषणं भवति (name the pollution type in Sanskrit)।
questions.explanation: Vehicle smoke causes air pollution — वायुप्रदूषणम्.

questions.question: मलिनजलेन विषाक्तरसायनैः च ____-प्रदूषणं जायते (name the pollution type in Sanskrit)।
questions.explanation: Sewage and toxic chemicals cause water pollution — जलप्रदूषणम्.

questions.question: 'वापी' इत्यस्य आङ्ग्लभाषायाम् अर्थः ____ (one English word/phrase)।
questions.explanation: वापी is a step-well; दश कूपसमा वापी — one step-well equals ten wells.

questions.question: 'नरकम्' इत्यस्य आङ्ग्लभाषायाम् अर्थः ____ (one English word)।
questions.explanation: नरकं न पश्येत् — the tree-planter never sees hell.

questions.question: संस्कृते 'tree' इत्यर्थे पदद्वयं पाठे आगतम् — वृक्षः तथा ____ ।
questions.explanation: Both वृक्षः and द्रुमः mean 'tree'; द्रुमः occurs in दशपुत्रसमो द्रुमः.

questions.question: भारतीयपरम्परायां नद्यः ____ पूज्यन्ते (adverb from the lesson meaning 'like a mother')।
questions.explanation: नद्यः मातृवत् पूज्यन्ते — rivers are worshipped like mothers.

questions.question: सन्धिविच्छेदं पूरयत — पुत्रोऽहम् = पुत्रः + ____ ।
questions.explanation: पुत्रः + अहम् = पुत्रोऽहम् (विसर्ग-सन्धि with अवग्रह).

questions.question: 'जलस्य प्रदूषणम्' इत्यस्य समस्तपदं लिखत — ____ ।
questions.explanation: जलस्य प्रदूषणम् = जलप्रदूषणम् (षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष compound).

questions.question: क्त्वान्तरूपेण पूरयत — वृक्षान् ____ सः जलम् अयच्छत् ('having planted', from रुह् causative रोपय-)।
questions.explanation: रोपयित्वा = 'having planted' — the क्त्वा absolutive of the causative रोपयति.

questions.question: 'वृक्षात्' इति पदे ____ विभक्तिः अस्ति (name the vibhakti)।
questions.explanation: वृक्षात् = 'from the tree' — the ablative, पञ्चमी विभक्तिः.

questions.question: Explain the formation (सन्धि) and meaning of the word पर्यावरणम्.
questions.answer: पर्यावरणम् = परि (around, on all sides) + आवरणम् (covering). By यण्-सन्धि the इ of परि combines with the following आ to become या (इ + आ = या). The word therefore means 'that which covers us on all sides' — the environment: the five elements together with trees, rivers, mountains, animals and birds.
questions.explanation: Tests both the yan-sandhi derivation and the sense of the chapter's title word.

questions.question: Name the पञ्चमहाभूतानि in Sanskrit and give the English meaning of each.
questions.answer: पृथिवी = earth; आपः (जलम्) = water; तेजः (अग्निः) = fire/energy; वायुः = air; आकाशः = space/sky. These five great elements are the basic constituents of the environment and of our own body.
questions.explanation: The five-element framework is the foundation of the chapter.

questions.question: 'पर्यावरणस्य रक्षा आत्मनः एव रक्षा' — Why does the lesson say that protecting the environment is protecting ourselves?
questions.answer: Because our body itself is पञ्चभूतात्मकम् — made of the same five elements (earth, water, fire, air, space) that constitute the environment. When the elements are pure and balanced, life flourishes; when they are polluted, disease and calamity strike every living being. Polluted air enters our lungs, polluted water our stomach, poisoned soil our food. Hence harming nature is self-harm, and conserving the elements is self-preservation — our धरणीधर्मः.
questions.explanation: Connects the panchamahabhuta doctrine to the logic of conservation.

questions.question: Write the meaning of the verse: दश कूपसमा वापी दशवापीसमो ह्रदः । दशह्रदसमः पुत्रो दशपुत्रसमो द्रुमः ॥
questions.answer: One step-well (वापी) is equal to ten wells (कूप); one lake (ह्रदः) is equal to ten step-wells; one son (पुत्रः) is equal to ten lakes; and one tree (द्रुमः) is equal to ten sons. The Matsya Purana thus builds a ladder of merit in which a single tree stands at the very top — above even ten sons.
questions.explanation: The verse ranks water-works, progeny and trees on a scale of public merit.

questions.question: Write the अन्वय (prose order) of the verse दश कूपसमा वापी दशवापीसमो ह्रदः । दशह्रदसमः पुत्रो दशपुत्रसमो द्रुमः ॥
questions.answer: अन्वय: वापी दशकूपसमा (भवति); ह्रदः दशवापीसमः (भवति); पुत्रः दशह्रदसमः (भवति); द्रुमः दशपुत्रसमः (भवति)। — A step-well equals ten wells, a lake ten step-wells, a son ten lakes, a tree ten sons.
questions.explanation: The anvaya simply supplies the copula भवति to each equation of the ladder.

questions.question: Which trees are named in the verse अश्वत्थमेकं पिचुमन्दमेकम्...? List them with their English names.
questions.answer: अश्वत्थः = peepal (one), पिचुमन्दः = neem (one), न्यग्रोधः = banyan (one), चिञ्चिणी = tamarind (ten), कपित्थः = wood-apple, बिल्वः = bael and आमलकः = amla (three of each), and आम्रः = mango (five). Planting these, the verse says, one never sees hell (नरकं न पश्येत्).
questions.explanation: Every tree in the list is of medicinal or nutritional value to the community.

questions.question: वायुप्रदूषणं किम्? तस्य कारणानि एकं परिणामं च लिखत। (What is air pollution? Give its causes and one effect.)
questions.answer: वायुप्रदूषणम् is the fouling of the air element. Its causes given in the lesson are the smoke of vehicles (यानानां धूमः), the smoke of factories (यन्त्रागाराणां धूमः) and the burning of forests (वनानां दहनम्). Its chief effect is that respiratory diseases arise (श्वासरोगाः जायन्ते) — the polluted air directly attacks the breath of life.
questions.explanation: Definition, three causes and effect exactly as in पाठ्यांश ४.

questions.question: State the sources and the two effects of ध्वनिप्रदूषणम् mentioned in the lesson.
questions.answer: Sources: the noise of vehicles (यानानां ध्वनिः) and blaring loudspeakers (उच्चैः वादित्राणि). Effects: the power of hearing diminishes (श्रवणशक्तिः हीयते) and the mind becomes restless (चित्तम् अशान्तं भवति).
questions.explanation: Noise pollution harms both body (hearing) and mind (peace).

questions.question: मृदाप्रदूषणस्य कारणे द्वे लिखत, एकम् उपायं च सूचयत। (Give two causes of soil pollution and suggest one remedy.)
questions.answer: Causes: plastic (प्लास्टिकम्) and chemical fertilizers (रासायनिकोर्वरकाणि), along with carelessly thrown garbage (अवकरः); these destroy the soil's fertility (उर्वरता नश्यति). Remedy: give up the use of plastic (प्लास्टिकस्य प्रयोगं त्यजेम), dispose of garbage properly, and prefer natural/organic manure over chemical fertilizers.
questions.explanation: Cause-and-remedy pairing from पाठ्यांश ४ and ५.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ (English meaning) of each: द्रुमः, पर्जन्यः, वापी, अवकरः, क्षिप्रम्.
questions.answer: द्रुमः = tree; पर्जन्यः = rain-cloud / rain; वापी = step-well; अवकरः = garbage, refuse; क्षिप्रम् = quickly.
questions.explanation: Core vocabulary from the verses and prose.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of each verb form: आवृणोति, पूज्यन्ते, म्रियन्ते, रोहतु, विखनामि.
questions.answer: आवृणोति = covers; पूज्यन्ते = are worshipped; म्रियन्ते = (they) die; रोहतु = may it grow (back); विखनामि = I dig out.
questions.explanation: Verbs drawn from पाठ्यांश १, ३ and the भूमिसूक्त lines.

questions.question: What do मितव्ययः and यन्त्रागारम् mean? Use each in a short Sanskrit sentence of your own.
questions.answer: मितव्ययः = measured/economical use; यन्त्रागारम् = factory. Example sentences: जलस्य मितव्ययः अस्माकं कर्तव्यम्। (Economical use of water is our duty.) यन्त्रागाराणां धूमः वायुं दूषयति। (The smoke of factories pollutes the air.)
questions.explanation: Vocabulary in active use — any grammatical sentence with the correct sense earns the marks.

questions.question: Why are rivers worshipped as mothers (मातृवत्) in Indian tradition? What ecological wisdom is hidden in this reverence?
questions.answer: Rivers are worshipped as mothers because, like a mother, they nourish life without asking anything in return — their water gives drink, irrigates crops (जलं विना न कृषिः न जीवनम्) and sustains whole civilisations settled on their banks. The ecological wisdom: what one reveres one does not defile. By making Ganga, Yamuna, Godavari and Kaveri sacred mothers, tradition built an inner restraint against polluting them — a cultural water-conservation system older than any environmental law.
questions.explanation: Links the religious attitude to its practical conservation function.

questions.question: What does the भूमिसूक्त prayer — यत् ते भूमे विखनामि क्षिप्रं तदपि रोहतु । मा ते मर्म विमृग्वरि मा ते हृदयमर्पिपम् ॥ — teach about the use of natural resources?
questions.answer: The seer asks that whatever he digs from the Earth may quickly grow back (क्षिप्रं तदपि रोहतु), and vows never to pierce her vitals or heart (मर्म, हृदयम्). The teaching: use the Earth only within her power of regeneration — take renewably, never wound her mortally by reckless mining, deforestation or exhaustion of the soil. It is the world's oldest statement of sustainable, restrained resource use, and it flows from seeing the Earth as one's own mother.
questions.explanation: The Vedic ethic of regeneration anticipates the modern idea of sustainability.

questions.question: Why did tradition link tree-planting with freedom from नरक (hell) in the verse अश्वत्थमेकं पिचुमन्दमेकम्...?
questions.answer: By promising that the planter of peepal, neem, banyan, tamarind and fruit trees 'never sees hell', tradition attached the highest spiritual reward to an ecological act. This converted tree-planting from an optional good deed into a sacred duty that ordinary people eagerly performed. The trees chosen are all of long life and great medicinal or nutritional value, so the 'merit' was in fact lasting public welfare.
questions.explanation: Religious motivation as a social engine for conservation.

questions.question: सन्धिविच्छेदं कुरुत, सन्धेः नाम च लिखत — (a) पर्यावरणम् (b) पुत्रोऽहम् (c) नास्ति।
questions.answer: (a) पर्यावरणम् = परि + आवरणम् — यण्-सन्धिः (इ + आ = या). (b) पुत्रोऽहम् = पुत्रः + अहम् — विसर्ग-सन्धिः (ः + अ = ोऽ, with अवग्रह). (c) नास्ति = न + अस्ति — सवर्णदीर्घ-सन्धिः (अ + अ = आ).
questions.explanation: Three different sandhi types from the chapter's own words.

questions.question: विग्रहं कृत्वा समासस्य नाम लिखत — (a) जलप्रदूषणम् (b) वृक्षारोपणम्।
questions.answer: (a) जलप्रदूषणम् = जलस्य प्रदूषणम् — षष्ठी-तत्पुरुषः (the pollution OF water). (b) वृक्षारोपणम् = वृक्षाणाम् आरोपणम् — षष्ठी-तत्पुरुषः (the planting OF trees).
questions.explanation: Both are genitive tatpurusha compounds, the commonest type in the chapter.

questions.question: State the विभक्ति (and number where relevant) of each word: वृक्षात्, नदीषु, जलेन, पृथिव्याः.
questions.answer: वृक्षात् — पञ्चमी एकवचनम् ('from the tree'); नदीषु — सप्तमी बहुवचनम् ('in the rivers'); जलेन — तृतीया एकवचनम् ('by water'); पृथिव्याः — षष्ठी एकवचनम् ('of the Earth').
questions.explanation: All four forms occur in the chapter's prose and verses.

questions.question: Explain the कृदन्त suffixes तुमुन् and क्त्वा with one example of each from this lesson.
questions.answer: तुमुन् forms the infinitive, 'in order to / to do': रक्षितुम् = 'to protect', as in पर्यावरणं रक्षितुं वयं वृक्षान् रोपयामः (to protect the environment we plant trees). क्त्वा forms the absolutive, 'having done': रोपयित्वा = 'having planted', as in वृक्षान् रोपयित्वा सः जलम् अयच्छत् (having planted the trees, he gave them water); similarly पीत्वा = 'having drunk' in दूषितं जलं पीत्वा.
questions.explanation: Infinitive of purpose vs. absolutive of prior action, both from chapter sentences.

questions.question: Translate into English: वयं वृक्षान् रोपयेम, जलं मितं व्ययेम, प्लास्टिकस्य प्रयोगं त्यजेम, अवकरं यत्र तत्र न क्षिपेम।
questions.answer: May we plant trees; may we use water sparingly; may we give up the use of plastic; may we not throw garbage here and there (may we never litter). The optative forms (रोपयेम, व्ययेम, त्यजेम, क्षिपेम) express gentle collective resolve — 'let us...'.
questions.explanation: The duties sentence of पाठ्यांश ५ with its optative verbs.

questions.question: Write any four duties (कर्तव्यानि) toward the environment taught in this lesson.
questions.answer: Any four of: (1) plant trees every year (वृक्षारोपणम्); (2) use water sparingly (जलस्य मितव्ययः); (3) give up plastic; (4) never throw garbage here and there; (5) prefer walking and cycling; (6) keep rivers clean; (7) inspire others to protect the environment.
questions.explanation: The duties list of पाठ्यांश ५ — the chapter's धरणीधर्मः.

questions.question: Translate the verse पृथिव्यां त्रीणि रत्नानि जलमन्नं सुभाषितम् । मूढैः पाषाणखण्डेषु रत्नसंज्ञा विधीयते ॥ and state its moral.
questions.answer: Translation: On this earth there are only three jewels — water, food and the well-spoken word; it is fools who apply the name 'jewel' to pieces of stone. Moral: the true wealth of the planet is what sustains life — water and food — not gold and gems; therefore conserving water and food is guarding the earth's real treasure.
questions.explanation: The subhashita redefines 'jewel' in ecological terms.

questions.question: Explain the पञ्चमहाभूत framework of the environment as given in this chapter, and evaluate how far this ancient framework agrees with the modern scientific view of the environment.
questions.answer: The chapter presents the environment as woven of five great elements: पृथिवी (earth/land), आपः (water), तेजः (fire/energy), वायुः (air) and आकाशः (space). Everything around us — and our own body, which is पञ्चभूतात्मकम् — is a combination of these. When the elements are pure and balanced, life flourishes; when polluted, disease and calamity follow. Evaluation: the framework maps remarkably well onto modern environmental science — पृथिवी corresponds to the lithosphere and soil, आपः to the hydrosphere, वायुः to the atmosphere, तेजः to solar and other energy, and आकाशः to space/the sound-carrying medium. The four pollutions of the lesson (मृदा, जल, वायु, ध्वनि) are exactly the degradations of these spheres. Where modern science adds detail (chemistry, ecosystems, climate systems), the ancient framework adds an ethical insight science lacks: since we are made of the same five elements, harming them is harming ourselves — making conservation a matter of self-preservation and dharma, not merely regulation.
questions.explanation: Requires both exposition of the doctrine and a reasoned comparison with the modern view.

questions.question: Write the verse दश कूपसमा वापी... in full and explain it completely — शब्दार्थ, अन्वय, translation and significance.
questions.answer: Verse (मत्स्यपुराणम्): दश कूपसमा वापी दशवापीसमो ह्रदः । दशह्रदसमः पुत्रो दशपुत्रसमो द्रुमः ॥ शब्दार्थ: कूपः = well; समा/समः = equal to; वापी = step-well; ह्रदः = lake; पुत्रः = son; द्रुमः = tree. अन्वय: वापी दशकूपसमा (भवति); ह्रदः दशवापीसमः; पुत्रः दशह्रदसमः; द्रुमः दशपुत्रसमः। Translation: one step-well equals ten wells; one lake equals ten step-wells; one son equals ten lakes; one tree equals ten sons. Significance: the verse builds a ladder of increasing public merit — from private wells to community step-wells to lakes, then to a son (who supports one family), and finally to the tree, which serves all beings — shade, fruit, oxygen, rain, shelter — selflessly for generations. Placing one tree above ten sons is the strongest possible statement of the ecological value of trees in ancient literature, and it turns tree-planting into the highest of charitable works.
questions.explanation: Full four-part treatment of the chapter's central verse.

questions.question: प्रदूषणं चतुर्विधं भवति — Explain the four kinds of pollution described in the lesson, giving for each its Sanskrit name, causes, effects and one remedy.
questions.answer: (1) वायुप्रदूषणम् (air pollution): caused by the smoke of vehicles and factories and the burning of forests; it produces respiratory diseases (श्वासरोगाः). Remedy: plant trees, prefer walking/cycling, control smoke. (2) जलप्रदूषणम् (water pollution): caused by city sewage (मलिनजलम्), poisonous chemicals of factories and garbage thrown into rivers; fish die and people fall ill by drinking foul water. Remedy: measured use of water, cleansing of rivers, no dumping of waste. (3) ध्वनिप्रदूषणम् (noise pollution): caused by the din of vehicles and blaring loudspeakers; hearing weakens (श्रवणशक्तिः हीयते) and the mind becomes restless. Remedy: avoid needless honking and loudspeakers. (4) मृदाप्रदूषणम् (soil pollution): caused by plastic, chemical fertilizers and garbage; the soil's fertility (उर्वरता) perishes. Remedy: give up plastic, use organic manure, dispose of waste properly. Together these show that every one of the five elements we depend on can be poisoned by human carelessness — and healed by human duty.
questions.explanation: The complete fourfold scheme of पाठ्यांश ४ with remedies from पाठ्यांश ५.

questions.question: Write the English meaning of each of these ten words from the chapter, and use any five of them in Sanskrit sentences of your own: वृक्षारोपणम्, मलिनजलम्, अवकरः, पर्जन्यः, द्रुमः, मितव्ययः, यन्त्रागारम्, श्वासरोगः, उर्वरता, आश्रयः.
questions.answer: Meanings: वृक्षारोपणम् = tree-planting; मलिनजलम् = sewage/dirty water; अवकरः = garbage; पर्जन्यः = rain-cloud/rain; द्रुमः = tree; मितव्ययः = economical use; यन्त्रागारम् = factory; श्वासरोगः = respiratory disease; उर्वरता = fertility (of soil); आश्रयः = shelter. Sample sentences (any five, any correct sentence accepted): (1) प्रतिवर्षं वृक्षारोपणं करणीयम्। (2) मलिनजलं नदीषु न पातनीयम्। (3) मार्गे अवकरः न क्षेप्तव्यः। (4) वृक्षाद् वर्षति पर्जन्यः। (5) जलस्य मितव्ययः सर्वैः करणीयः। (6) यन्त्रागाराणां धूमः वायुं दूषयति। (7) वृक्षाः पक्षिभ्यः आश्रयं ददति।
questions.explanation: Vocabulary mastery shown both by translation and by active use in sentences.

questions.question: 'भारतीयपरम्परा पर्यावरणरक्षायाः आदिगुरुः' — Analyse how Indian tradition (the भूमिसूक्त, river-worship, and the tree-verses of the Puranas) encodes environmental ethics, and discuss whether this heritage is relevant to today's environmental crisis.
questions.answer: Indian tradition embedded conservation inside religion and daily conduct. (1) The भूमिसूक्त of the Atharvaveda declares माता भूमिः पुत्रोऽहं पृथिव्याः — the Earth is a mother, not a commodity — and the seer vows to dig only what can quickly regrow and never to pierce her vitals: the principle of sustainable, regenerative use. (2) Rivers are worshipped मातृवत् — what one reveres one does not defile; sacredness acted as an inner pollution-control on Ganga, Yamuna and the rest. (3) The Purana verses make the tree the summit of merit (दशपुत्रसमो द्रुमः) and promise the planter of peepal, neem, banyan and fruit trees freedom from hell — converting afforestation into a mass religious practice. Relevance today: the crisis of climate, dying rivers and vanishing forests is at root a crisis of attitude — nature seen as raw material. The traditional attitude of kinship and reverence supplies the missing motivation that laws alone cannot: if the Earth is mother, pollution becomes matricide and conservation becomes filial duty. Joined to modern science and technology, this heritage is not nostalgia but a working ethic — as movements like Chipko and river-rejuvenation campaigns rooted in these very sentiments show.
questions.explanation: Analysis of three strands of tradition plus a reasoned judgement on modern relevance.

questions.question: From this chapter explain with examples: (a) यण्-सन्धि, (b) जश्त्व-सन्धि, (c) विसर्ग-सन्धि; and (d) give the विग्रह and name of the समास of वायुप्रदूषणम् and महाभूतम्.
questions.answer: (a) यण्-सन्धिः: a simple vowel (इ/उ/ऋ) before a dissimilar vowel becomes its semivowel — परि + आवरणम् = पर्यावरणम् (इ + आ → या). (b) जश्त्व-सन्धिः: a final hard consonant becomes its soft (voiced) counterpart before a voiced sound — वृक्षात् + वर्षति = वृक्षाद् वर्षति and पर्जन्यात् + अन्नसम्भवः = पर्जन्यादन्नसम्भवः (त् → द्). (c) विसर्ग-सन्धिः: visarga after अ becomes ओ before a voiced consonant — दशपुत्रसमः + द्रुमः = दशपुत्रसमो द्रुमः; and with a following अ it yields ोऽ — पुत्रः + अहम् = पुत्रोऽहम् (the अवग्रह ऽ marks the lost अ). (d) वायुप्रदूषणम् = वायोः प्रदूषणम् — षष्ठी-तत्पुरुषः (the pollution OF air); महाभूतम् = महत् च तत् भूतम् — कर्मधारयः (adjective + noun in apposition).
questions.explanation: All examples are drawn from the chapter's own words and verses.

questions.question: Explain the four कृदन्त forms taught in this chapter — तुमुन्, क्त्वा, ल्यप् and क्त — with one example of each from the lesson, and state the विभक्ति of: पक्षिभ्यः, पृथिव्याम्, हे भूमे.
questions.answer: कृदन्ताः: (1) तुमुन् — infinitive of purpose, 'to / in order to': रक्षितुम् (पर्यावरणं रक्षितुं वयं वृक्षान् रोपयामः — to protect the environment we plant trees). (2) क्त्वा — absolutive, 'having done' (simple verb): रोपयित्वा (वृक्षान् रोपयित्वा — having planted trees); पीत्वा (दूषितं जलं पीत्वा — having drunk polluted water). (3) ल्यप् — absolutive of a prefixed verb: संरक्ष्य (नदीं संरक्ष्य ग्रामः सुखी अभवत् — having protected the river, the village became happy). (4) क्त — past passive participle: प्रदूषितम् = 'polluted', रक्षितम् = 'protected'. विभक्तिः: पक्षिभ्यः — चतुर्थी बहुवचनम् ('for the birds', as in पक्षिभ्यः आश्रयं ददति); पृथिव्याम् — सप्तमी एकवचनम् ('on the earth', as in पृथिव्यां त्रीणि रत्नानि); हे भूमे — सम्बोधनम् ('O Earth!', as in यत् ते भूमे विखनामि).
questions.explanation: Covers all kridanta types and three case-forms straight from the text.

questions.question: 'पर्यावरणस्य संरक्षणम् अस्माकं कर्तव्यम्' — इति विषये पञ्च-षट् वाक्यैः संस्कृतेन एकम् अनुच्छेदं लिखत। (Write a short Sanskrit paragraph of 5–6 sentences on 'Protection of the environment is our duty'. An English gloss may be added.)
questions.answer: Model paragraph: पर्यावरणं पञ्चमहाभूतैः निर्मितम् अस्ति। वृक्षाः नद्यः च अस्माकं जीवनस्य आधाराः सन्ति। परं मानवः स्वार्थेन वायुं जलं भूमिं च दूषयति। अतः वयं प्रतिवर्षं वृक्षान् रोपयेम, जलं मितं व्ययेम, प्लास्टिकस्य प्रयोगं त्यजेम। माता भूमिः, वयं तस्याः पुत्राः — इति भावेन प्रकृतिं रक्षेम। पर्यावरणस्य रक्षा एव अस्माकं रक्षा, एषः एव धरणीधर्मः। (Gloss: The environment is made of the five elements; trees and rivers are the supports of our life; but man pollutes air, water and land out of selfishness; therefore let us plant trees yearly, use water sparingly and give up plastic; with the feeling 'Earth is our mother, we her children' let us protect nature; the protection of the environment is our own protection — this is our dharma to the Earth.) Any coherent, grammatical paragraph covering the theme earns full marks.
questions.explanation: Free composition in Sanskrit applying the chapter's vocabulary, grammar and ideas.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
दश कूपसमा वापी दशवापीसमो ह्रदः ।
दशह्रदसमः पुत्रो दशपुत्रसमो द्रुमः ॥
(a) From which text is this verse taken? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of वापी and ह्रदः. (c) What equals ten sons? (d) State the message of the verse.
questions.answer: (a) From the मत्स्यपुराणम् (Matsya Purana). (b) वापी = step-well; ह्रदः = lake/large pond. (c) One tree (द्रुमः) equals ten sons — दशपुत्रसमो द्रुमः. (d) Message: merit increases from wells to step-wells to lakes to a son, and a single tree stands above them all — planting and protecting trees is the highest public good.
questions.explanation: Source, vocabulary, recall and message of the chapter's key verse.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
अश्वत्थमेकं पिचुमन्दमेकं न्यग्रोधमेकं दश चिञ्चिणीकान् ।
कपित्थबिल्वामलकत्रयं च पञ्चाम्रवापी नरकं न पश्येत् ॥
(a) Name the three trees to be planted one each. (b) How many mango trees are mentioned? (c) What reward does the verse promise? (d) Why do you think only useful (medicinal/fruit) trees are listed?
questions.answer: (a) One each of अश्वत्थ (peepal), पिचुमन्द (neem) and न्यग्रोध (banyan). (b) Five mango trees (पञ्च आम्राः, in पञ्चाम्रवापी). (c) The planter 'never sees hell' — नरकं न पश्येत्. (d) Because the aim is lasting public welfare: peepal and banyan give abundant shade and oxygen and live for centuries, neem and bael and amla are medicinal, tamarind and mango and wood-apple feed generations — so the promised 'merit' is in reality permanent service to the whole community.
questions.explanation: Comprehension plus a reasoning step about the selection of species.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
अद्य नगराणां मलिनजलं यन्त्रागाराणां च विषाक्तं द्रव्यं नदीषु पात्यते। तेन जलप्रदूषणं जायते, मत्स्याः म्रियन्ते, जनाः रोगैः पीड्यन्ते।
(a) What two things are dumped into the rivers? (b) What pollution arises from this? (c) State the two consequences given. (d) Give the शब्दार्थ of पात्यते.
questions.answer: (a) The sewage of cities (नगराणां मलिनजलम्) and the poisonous discharge of factories (यन्त्रागाराणां विषाक्तं द्रव्यम्). (b) जलप्रदूषणम् — water pollution. (c) Fish die (मत्स्याः म्रियन्ते) and people are afflicted by diseases (जनाः रोगैः पीड्यन्ते). (d) पात्यते = 'is thrown/dumped' (passive causative of पत्).
questions.explanation: Direct comprehension of the water-pollution passage of पाठ्यांश ३.

questions.question:
Read the भूमिसूक्त lines and answer:
माता भूमिः पुत्रोऽहं पृथिव्याः ।
यत् ते भूमे विखनामि क्षिप्रं तदपि रोहतु ।
मा ते मर्म विमृग्वरि मा ते हृदयमर्पिपम् ॥
(a) In which Veda do these lines occur? (b) What relationship is declared in the first line? (c) What two promises/prayers does the seer make about digging? (d) Which modern environmental principle do these lines anticipate?
questions.answer: (a) In the अथर्ववेद (the भूमिसूक्त, Hymn to the Earth). (b) The Earth is the mother and the speaker is her son — माता भूमिः पुत्रोऽहं पृथिव्याः. (c) That whatever he digs may quickly grow back (क्षिप्रं तदपि रोहतु), and that he may never pierce the Earth's vitals or heart (मा ते मर्म... मा ते हृदयम्). (d) The principle of sustainability — using natural resources only within their power of regeneration, never wounding the Earth beyond recovery.
questions.explanation: Source, relationship, content and modern parallel of the Vedic prayer.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
भारतीयपरम्परायां नद्यः मातृवत् पूज्यन्ते — गङ्गा यमुना गोदावरी सरस्वती नर्मदा सिन्धुः कावेरी च। 'जलं जीवनम्' इति सर्वे जानन्ति।
(a) How are rivers regarded in Indian tradition? (b) Name any four rivers from the passage. (c) What does 'जलं जीवनम्' mean? (d) How does this reverence help conservation?
questions.answer: (a) Rivers are worshipped like mothers (मातृवत् पूज्यन्ते). (b) Any four of: गङ्गा, यमुना, गोदावरी, सरस्वती, नर्मदा, सिन्धुः, कावेरी. (c) 'Water is life' — without water there is no agriculture and no life. (d) What people revere they do not defile: treating rivers as sacred mothers creates an inner restraint against polluting them and a duty to keep them clean — a cultural system of water conservation.
questions.explanation: Comprehension plus analysis of the conservation function of reverence.

questions.question:
Read the line and answer:
वृक्षाद् वर्षति पर्जन्यः पर्जन्यादन्नसम्भवः ।
(a) Split the सन्धि in वृक्षाद् वर्षति and name it. (b) Split पर्जन्यादन्नसम्भवः. (c) Which विभक्ति is वृक्षात् and why? (d) Translate the line.
questions.answer: (a) वृक्षात् + वर्षति — जश्त्व-सन्धिः (final त् becomes द् before the voiced व्). (b) पर्जन्यात् + अन्नसम्भवः (again त् → द् before the vowel अ). (c) वृक्षात् is पञ्चमी (ablative), because it expresses the source — 'FROM (because of) the tree'. (d) Translation: Because of trees the rain-cloud rains; from rain arises food.
questions.explanation: Grammar and translation combined on a single chapter line.

questions.question:
Read the sentence and answer:
पर्यावरणं रक्षितुं वयं वृक्षान् रोपयित्वा जलं यच्छामः।
(a) Identify the तुमुन् form and give its meaning. (b) Identify the क्त्वा form and give its meaning. (c) Which विभक्ति is वृक्षान्? (d) Translate the whole sentence.
questions.answer: (a) रक्षितुम् — तुमुन् (infinitive), 'in order to protect'. (b) रोपयित्वा — क्त्वा (absolutive), 'having planted'. (c) वृक्षान् is द्वितीया बहुवचनम् (accusative plural) — the object 'trees'. (d) Translation: In order to protect the environment, we plant trees and (having planted them) give them water.
questions.explanation: Applies the chapter's kridanta and vibhakti teaching to one sentence.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
वयं वृक्षान् रोपयेम, जलं मितं व्ययेम, प्लास्टिकस्य प्रयोगं त्यजेम, अवकरं यत्र तत्र न क्षिपेम, अन्यान् अपि पर्यावरणरक्षायै प्रेरयेम।
(a) List the five duties stated. (b) What mood are the verbs रोपयेम, व्ययेम, त्यजेम in, and what does it express? (c) Give the शब्दार्थ of अवकरः. (d) What does the lesson call this set of duties?
questions.answer: (a) Plant trees; use water sparingly; give up the use of plastic; not throw garbage here and there; inspire others also to protect the environment. (b) They are optative (विधिलिङ्, 'may we...'), expressing gentle collective resolve/duty. (c) अवकरः = garbage, refuse. (d) The lesson calls this our धरणीधर्मः — the dharma owed to the Earth.
questions.explanation: Comprehension of the duties passage with a grammar observation.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
पृथिव्यां त्रीणि रत्नानि जलमन्नं सुभाषितम् ।
मूढैः पाषाणखण्डेषु रत्नसंज्ञा विधीयते ॥
(a) Name the three jewels. (b) Who applies the name 'jewel' to stones? (c) Which विभक्ति is पृथिव्याम्? (d) How does this verse support water conservation?
questions.answer: (a) जलम् (water), अन्नम् (food) and सुभाषितम् (the well-said word). (b) मूढाः — fools (मूढैः, 'by fools'). (c) पृथिव्याम् is सप्तमी एकवचनम् (locative) — 'on the earth'. (d) By counting water among the earth's only three true jewels, the verse teaches that water — not gold or gems — is real wealth; a jewel is guarded and never wasted, so water too must be conserved drop by drop.
questions.explanation: Comprehension, grammar and the conservation moral of the subhashita.

questions.question:
Case: A factory (यन्त्रागारम्) near a village releases its poisonous discharge into the river from which the villagers drink; fish are dying and children are falling ill. The village council asks students of this chapter for advice.
(a) Name the pollution involved (Sanskrit term). (b) Which two effects mentioned in the lesson are already visible? (c) Quote one line from the chapter's tradition (verse or sukta) that the students could cite. (d) Suggest three practical steps for the village, in the spirit of the lesson.
questions.answer: (a) जलप्रदूषणम् (water pollution), caused by the यन्त्रागारस्य विषाक्तं द्रव्यम्. (b) मत्स्याः म्रियन्ते (fish are dying) and जनाः रोगैः पीड्यन्ते (people are afflicted by disease). (c) Any one: 'माता भूमिः पुत्रोऽहं पृथिव्याः' (the Earth/river is our mother — she must not be poisoned); or 'जलं जीवनम्'; or 'पृथिव्यां त्रीणि रत्नानि जलमन्नं सुभाषितम्'. (d) Steps: demand that the factory treat/stop its discharge before it reaches the river; organise river-cleaning (नदीनां शुद्धिः) and stop the village's own sewage and garbage from entering the water; secure clean drinking water and plant trees along the banks; and spread awareness — अन्यान् अपि पर्यावरणरक्षायै प्रेरयेम.
questions.explanation: Applies the chapter's terms, verses and duties to a realistic scenario.
